scenarios.search_intent: Classify incoming reference queries into appropriate administrative departments.
scenarios.summary: Automated routing of digital library reference requests to specialized archival or research teams.
scenarios.problem: Public library systems receive diverse user queries that often span multiple subjects. Manual sorting results in frequent misrouting of interdisciplinary requests and increased administrative overhead. The application must analyze the query text and provide a consistent department selection to trigger an automated ticketing system update.
scenarios.input_description: A user-submitted query text string regarding research assistance.
scenarios.decision: Choice: Map the input to a specific department (e.g., genealogy, digital-media, technical-services) or route to manual review.
scenarios.action: Downstream code updates the ticketing system status and routes the request to the chosen department queue.

scenarios.search_intent: Check whether software license request justifications include a purpose and project reference.
scenarios.summary: Triage software license requests for missing business context before procurement review.
scenarios.problem: Software license requests often arrive with vague justifications. A procurement reviewer needs a stated purpose and project reference before checking budget, entitlement and approval rules. This example checks whether the submitted text supplies those two details so the application can request missing information first.
scenarios.input_description: The 'justification' field submitted in the procurement form.
scenarios.decision: Noul: Does the justification state a concrete work purpose and include a specific project identifier?
scenarios.action: Send sufficiently complete requests to procurement review; ask the requester for more detail when the justification is incomplete.

scenarios.search_intent: Screen raw material specification sheets for undeclared allergen risks.
scenarios.summary: Triage supplier ingredient specification sheets to flag potential unlabeled common food allergens before inventory intake.
scenarios.problem: The input provides supplier-submitted ingredient compositions, processing aid descriptions, and facility handling statements. Suppliers use varied phrasing for cross-contact risks, making basic keyword searches prone to confusing trace warnings with active ingredients or omitting unmentioned allergens entirely. The application must classify the text disclosure so downstream services can route ambiguous or incomplete records to specialists for review before intake. This text-based triage evaluates only what the supplier documented; it does not replace independent laboratory testing or authoritative verification of facility sanitation.
scenarios.input_description: A JSON object containing the supplier ingredient notes, facility handling notes, and stated composition.
scenarios.decision: Choice: Classify the ingredient profile into allergen-free-declared, allergen-present-declared, ambiguous-trace-warning, or missing-disclosure.
scenarios.action: Downstream code marks the batch profile for immediate warehouse release, routes it to an allergen specialist for audit, or returns the form to the supplier requesting missing documentation.

scenarios.search_intent: Score tenant maintenance requests to identify urgent building safety hazards versus routine repairs.
scenarios.summary: Score the operational urgency of commercial tenant maintenance work orders to prioritize technician dispatch.
scenarios.problem: The system receives a JSON payload detailing the tenant issue description, affected room type, and reported operational impact. Critical issues like active leaks or sparking electrical panels easily get buried behind non-urgent cosmetic requests when dispatchers face heavy ticket volume. Your application must evaluate the stated severity from the submitted text so downstream dispatch rules can prioritize technician paging for urgent hazards.
scenarios.input_description: A JSON object containing the tenant issue description, affected room type, and reported impact on daily business.
scenarios.decision: Score: Score the reported hazard severity from 0 (purely aesthetic preference) to 4 (immediate life safety hazard or uncontrolled flooding).
scenarios.action: Work order software automatically triggers immediate on-call technician paging for high-severity scores or enqueues the request in the regular maintenance queue.

scenarios.search_intent: Score the descriptive thoroughness of wind turbine gearbox lubrication field service reports.
scenarios.summary: Evaluate technician maintenance log entries for comprehensive component inspection and measurement notes.
scenarios.problem: Field technicians submit a free-text maintenance work summary after completing gearbox lubrication servicing under demanding site conditions. Summaries often leave out critical quantitative readings, such as particulate counts or viscosity values, or fail to describe mechanical seal conditions. The asset management application must evaluate the descriptive completeness of these notes so incomplete logs can be flagged for technician revision before review. Because text thoroughness does not verify mechanical safety or replace physical inspections, the application uses this score solely for documentation triage.
scenarios.input_description: The maintenance_work_summary text submitted by the field technician upon service completion.
scenarios.decision: Score: Score report completeness on three levels: 0 (insufficient summary lacking specific component observations), 1 (basic summary with qualitative notes but missing physical measurements), and 2 (thorough report detailing component conditions and quantitative readings).
scenarios.action: Utility asset management software marks the technician work order as completed for score 2 or prevents work order sign-off and notifies the technician to enrich their notes for scores 0 and 1.

scenarios.search_intent: Map playlist mood descriptions to colour palettes
scenarios.summary: Map an emotive playlist description to the colour palette archetype it evokes.
scenarios.problem: The application receives a short free-text atmosphere description written by a user or playlist curator. Traditional metadata like genre, tempo, or release year does not reveal whether a playlist feels like a neon synthwave night or a golden sunset afternoon. The application must evaluate the ambient description against candidate palette definitions and choose the matching archetype or select a neutral default theme. Downstream code then uses this evaluation to update player UI styling dynamically.
scenarios.input_description: A short free-text playlist atmosphere description.
scenarios.decision: Choose the colour palette archetype (neon synthwave, earthy acoustic, pastel lofi, golden sunset) the description evokes.
scenarios.action: Apply the matching colour theme to the player interface.

scenarios.search_intent: Score culinary recipe spice and heat level from short dish descriptions.
scenarios.summary: Score the heat level of home cooking descriptions to drive interactive flame gauge animations.
scenarios.problem: The input context contains custom ingredient lists or short preparation notes submitted by users. Simple keyword matching fails to accurately reflect net spice levels when recipes combine multiple hot peppers or add neutralizing elements like sour cream. The application must analyze the overall written profile to estimate relative heat intensity without relying on rigid keyword lists.
scenarios.input_description: A short free-text dish description or ingredient combination written by a home cook.
scenarios.decision: Score: Rate reported heat intensity across 5 levels from 0 (mild / zero spice) to 4 (extreme fire / pepperhead).
scenarios.action: Downstream code animates a heat gauge UI component and displays appropriate spice indicator icons.
